gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 13 build now compiles the first Landlock syscall helper lab beside the existing ruleset, libfs, and devres slices so this security-helper lane is reviewable without pretending it belongs in the live kernel build yet.
The existing Phase 13 make target keeps the bounded Landlock syscall helper lab runnable through the same repeatable tranche gate as the other shared-helper lanes.

The first honest `syscalls.zig` foothold stays in-memory around `build_check_abi()`, `landlock_create_ruleset()`, and `landlock_restrict_self()` so Zigux can model ABI sizing, query handling, mask validation, and logging-flag translation before any file-descriptor lookup, path import, or credential mutation is attempted.
A dedicated Phase 13 test gate now checks both the helper behavior and the survey manifest so future runs can see the narrow syscall starter and the still-missing kernel state in one place.

The dedicated reviewability gate now keeps the helper surface, manifest, survey note, and shared Phase 13 build wiring aligned so future runs can detect packet drift before widening into live file-descriptor or credential state.
The slice note records the exact helper-first boundary of the new syscall lab so the lane does not overstate ABI and flag planning as live syscall plumbing.
The survey note compares the 592-line `syscalls.c` anchor against the new starter and keeps the remaining gap around rule insertion, file descriptors, path import, and credential changes explicit.

The syscall helper now includes one tiny in-memory planner around `is_initialized()` so Zigux keeps the shared `-EOPNOTSUPP` boot-disabled gate and warning-once intent explicit before any create-ruleset, add-rule, or restrict-self path widens into live setup state.

The syscall helper now includes one small in-memory planner around `copy_min_struct_from_user()` so Zigux makes the null-user rejection, minimum-size and page-limit checks, and copy-then-zero-fill intent explicit before any live user-memory access is attempted.

The syscall helper now includes one small in-memory planner around `landlock_add_rule()` rule-type dispatch, empty-access rejection, and net-port bounds so Zigux can capture rule-shape validation before any real ruleset FD validation or path resolution is attempted.

The syscall helper now includes one small in-memory planner around `get_ruleset_from_fd()` bad-FD rejection, ruleset-FD type checks, `FMODE_CAN_WRITE` or `FMODE_CAN_READ` access checks, and the single-layer guard so Zigux can model the shared read-versus-write gate before any path-backed rule import, credential updates, or live domain state.

The syscall helper now includes one small in-memory planner around `get_path_from_fd()` rejecting ruleset FDs, internal mounts, and private or non-user-visible inodes while still modeling the owned path reference handoff before any path-backed rule import, credential updates, or live domain state.

The syscall helper now includes one tiny in-memory planner around `add_rule_path_beneath()` that combines copied path-beneath attrs with the bounded `get_path_from_fd()` handoff and the later `put_path()` release responsibility before any live rule insertion or inode ownership changes are attempted.

The syscall helper now includes one tiny in-memory planner around `add_rule_net_port()` that keeps copied net-port attrs, reused add-rule validation, and the final `landlock_append_net_rule()` handoff explicit before any live TCP/IP, ruleset mutation, or domain state are attempted.

The syscall helper now includes one tiny in-memory planner around `anon_inode_getfd()` that keeps the fixed `[landlock-ruleset]` label, `O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC` flags, and the `landlock_put_ruleset()` failure release discipline explicit before any live file operations wiring or FD ownership is attempted.

The syscall helper now includes one tiny in-memory planner around `prepare_creds()`, `landlock_merge_ruleset()`, optional sibling-thread synchronization, and `commit_creds()` so Zigux keeps the bounded restrict-self credential handoff order explicit before any live credential mutation or domain ownership is attempted.

The syscall helper now keeps the dedicated `ruleset_fops` contract explicit by recording the `fop_ruleset_release()` ownership drop and the dummy read or write handlers that enable `FMODE_CAN_READ` and `FMODE_CAN_WRITE` before any live file operations wiring or FD ownership is attempted.
